newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila rules out mediation role in East Timor.
newsitem.headline: Manila rules out mediation role in East Timor.

text.p: The Philippines on Wednesday brushed aside suggestions it could help mediate the dispute between Indonesia and East Timor, saying it did not want to put its nose in Jakarta's affairs.

Nobel peace laureate Jose Ramos-Horta, leader of a group opposed to Indonesia's occupation of the former Portuguese colony, said in Sydney on Tuesday Manila could help broker a settlement in East Timor, being a close ally of Indonesia.
"We would not want to interfere in the internal affairs of other countries," Ramos told his weekly news conference.
Ramos also said he was standing firm on his decision to bar the entry of Ramos-Horta to the Philippines during the November 25 summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
Ramos said the East Timorese dissident's presence in the country "is inimical to our national interests".
Indonesia helped mediate talks that led to the signing last month of a peace accord between Manila and Moslem separatists in the southern Philippines.
